title: Compact-source slices in an accessible infinity category
statement: Use the universes, smallness, compactness and filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the coherent functors, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe, let $\mathcal C$ be a $\kappa$-accessible quasicategory, and let $D\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the replete full subcategory of all $\kappa$-compact objects. Then $D$ is essentially small. For each $x\in\mathcal C$, the coherent slice $\mathcal C_{/x}$ has arrows $c\to x$ as objects and commuting triangles over the identity of x as morphisms, retaining all higher coherent homotopies. Define $D_{/x}$ to be its full subcategory on arrows $d\to x$ with $d\in D$. Then $D_{/x}$ is essentially small and $\kappa$-filtered. Its source projection $D_{/x}\to D\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$, with the tautological cocone to $x$, is a colimit diagram. Colimits indexed by $D_{/x}$ mean colimits after passage to a small equivalent quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.2(2)-(3), Lemma 5.4.2.4, Corollary 5.3.5.4 and Lemma 5.1.5.3: the canonical compact-source slice under an object after the Ind presentation of an accessible category. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent result.

proof.text: By accessibility choose an essentially small full subcategory $G\subseteq\mathcal C$ of $\kappa$-compact generators. If $d\in D$, choose its small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $F:I\to G$ with colimit $d$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-compact-stage-factorization] to $1_d$: there are $d\xrightarrow{v}F(i)\xrightarrow{r}d$ with $rv$ homotopic to $1_d$. Thus $D$ is contained in the replete full subcategory of homotopy retracts of objects of $G$, which is essentially small by [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus]. A full replete subcategory of an essentially small category is essentially small: take the full subcategory of a small representative on the objects whose images lie in $D$, and restrict the equivalence. This proves the first assertion without claiming that every compact object belongs to the original generator family.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.2(3) and the homotopy-retract argument of Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp. 424-425; Proposition 5.4.1.7 for size.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections] with the essentially small replete full subcategory $D$, the one-point simplicial set $K=\Delta^0$, and $p$ selecting $x$. Its category of sections is precisely the coherent category of pairs $(d,d\to x)$, hence $D_{/x}$, and the cited essential-smallness clause makes it essentially small. Fix a small equivalent quasicategory $S\simeq D_{/x}$ for all later uses of small-index colimits and cofinality. Work with the original slice when constructing cones, and transport along this equivalence when a small index is required. An equivalence and its coherent quasi-inverse transport cones and their universal properties, so this choice changes no assertion.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7 and the relative-slice construction in Proposition 5.4.4.3, with base a point; local smallness is part of accessibility.

proof.text: Choose a small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $F:I\to G\subseteq D$ of $x$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-kappa-poset] to $I$: there are a small nonempty partially ordered set $A$, in which every subset of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has an upper bound, and $u:N(A)\to I$. The cited node asserts colimit invariance for targets admitting all small colimits; do not assume that $\mathcal C$ is such a target. Instead apply that assertion to every diagram $I\to\mathcal S$, where small colimits of spaces exist by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. This is condition (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], so its condition (3) gives weak contractibility of all $(i\downarrow u)$. Now [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion], which requires no colimit-existence condition on the target, implies that the given colimiting cocone on $F$ restricts to a colimiting cocone on $p=Fu:N(A)\to D$, with the same apex $x$. The dual of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], applied in the opposite quasicategory, represents this coherent cocone by a join cocone $\bar p:N(A)^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$, with cone vertex $x$; its comparison preserves the source diagram, the vertex and the colimit property. Use this induced coherent cocone to define $q:N(A)\to D_{/x}$, sending $a$ to its leg $p(a)\to x$ with the coherent triangles. Compose with a quasi-inverse $D_{/x}\to S$ whenever using the small representative.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.18 (April 2017 numbering; Proposition 5.3.1.16 in the 2012 text cited by the poset node); join-versus-coherent cocone comparison.

proof.text: To prove $\kappa$-filteredness, take any $\kappa$-small simplicial set $K$, including $\varnothing$, and any diagram $h:K\to D_{/x}$. Use a quasi-inverse of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] to obtain an equivalent diagram in the join slice, still with sources in $D$ since $D$ is replete and the comparison is over $\mathcal C$. Unpacking this join-slice diagram gives $u:K\star\{\infty\}\to\mathcal C$ with apex $x$ and source diagram $d:K\to D$. Apply [lem-coef-compact-relative-cocone-factorization] to $K'=\varnothing\subseteq K$, this $d$, the presentation $\bar p$ of step 3, $r=\bar p$ (the join with the empty set is the other factor), and the cocone $u$. Every vertex of $d$ is $\kappa$-compact, the indexing poset has the required upper bounds, and both cocones have the same apex $x$, so all hypotheses hold. The result is $v:K\star\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$, restricting to $d$ on $K$, to $u$ on $K\star\{1\}$, and to $p(a)\to x$ on $\Delta^1$ for some $a\in A$. Since $K\star\Delta^1=(K\star\Delta^0)\star\Delta^0$, with the last vertex interpreted as $x$, this is exactly a join-slice cocone on the chosen diagram, with new vertex $p(a)\to x$. Its sources lie in $D$, so fullness puts the cocone in the compact-source slice. Apply the slice comparison back and compose with the coherent equivalence of boundary diagrams to obtain a cocone on $h$. For $K=\varnothing$ the construction produces the object $p(a)\to x$, proving nonemptiness as well. This verifies the defining cone condition for $D_{/x}$, and hence for its small representative $S$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14 and the relative lifting argument of Lemma 5.5.4.13, specialized to empty prescribed subdiagram; Kerodon slice diagonal comparison.

proof.text:
We next show that the presentation functor $q$ is cofinal; this also keeps track of the specific tautological cocone. Fix $b=(d\xrightarrow{f}x)\in D_{/x}$ and put $B=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(d,x)$. The cone mapping-space formula in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], with the fixed target diagram the point $x$, identifies naturally in $a$
$$\operatorname{Map}_{D_{/x}}(b,q(a))\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{f}\big(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(d,p(a))\longrightarrow B\big).$$
Fullness of $D_{/x}$ gives the same mapping space as the ambient slice. All computations may be made in the larger space universe, where these mapping spaces are small; $N(A)$ is small there too. By $\kappa$-compactness of $d$, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_a\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(d,p(a))\to B$ induced by the legs of $\bar p$ is an equivalence. Small colimits of these spaces exist by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. By the constant-diagram and filtered-contractibility clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula], applied to the infinity category of spaces, the identity cocones on the constant diagrams $B$ and $\{f\}\simeq *$ are colimiting. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] to the finite pullback shape defining the homotopy fiber; this shape is $\kappa$-small even for $\kappa=\aleph_0$. It follows that
$$\operatorname{colim}_{a\in N(A)}\operatorname{Map}_{D_{/x}}(b,q(a))\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{f}(B\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}B)\simeq *.$$
The middle map is the canonical compactness equivalence, identified with the identity of $B$; it is not an arbitrary map between equivalent spaces. The last fiber is contractible: its points are a point of $B$ together with a path to $f$, and this path space contracts to the constant path at $f$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3.3 (filtered colimits commute with small limits), compactness Definition 5.3.4.5, and the slice mapping-space fiber calculation; the cofinal compact-presentation argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Transfer the mapping-space calculation of step 5 across $S\simeq D_{/x}$; equivalences induce equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For the resulting functor $q_S:N(A)\to S$, condition (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test] holds for every object of $S$. Its equivalent condition (3) says that every coherent comma category $(s\downarrow q_S)$ is weakly contractible. Now apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] to $q_S$ and the source diagram $H:S\to D_{/x}\to\mathcal C$. This theorem identifies coherent cocone categories over $\mathcal C$, and says a given cocone is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $q_S$ is. The restriction of the tautological cocone $H\to x$ is the chosen presentation cocone $p\to x$, up to the coherent equivalences used above, and it is colimiting by step 3. Thus the tautological cocone itself is colimiting. This proves the claimed colimit with apex $x$ using a small representative of $D_{/x}$ and without assuming that $\mathcal C$ has any colimits other than its given small $\kappa$-filtered ones.
